claude.rationale: This is not a discrete merger/acquisition but an externally managed non-traded REIT: the registrant owns the customer-facing product (the pooled net-leased data center/healthcare portfolio, 51 properties held through wholly-owned single-purpose subsidiaries) but "has no paid employees" and "rel[ies] on our Advisor to provide substantially all of our services" — so the operational processes (property/asset management) never cross the ownership boundary into the registrant, driving gap_45=1. Likewise T6 organization/people are entirely absent from the registrant (no employees; management supplied by the Sponsor/Advisor/Property Manager complex), so the processes run without an internal organization aligned alongside them, driving gap_56=1. Both gaps are contractually absorbed via the Advisory Agreement and Property Management arrangement allocating the external substrate, so gap_mitigated=yes.

gemini.rationale: The provided slice describes a continuously offered, non-traded REIT with ongoing property acquisitions rather than a discrete M&A transaction crossing an ownership boundary. Therefore, no structural transfer or gaps can be determined from the closing-era evidence.

openai.rationale: The customer-facing assets were accumulated into a diversified pool through ongoing property acquisitions, while property and asset management were supplied alongside that pool by the external Advisor and Property Manager under an Advisory Agreement; therefore, no product-versus-process structural mismatch is documented. [SRC: SEC accession 0001567925-17-000028, Form 10-K FY2016] The registrant had no paid employees and relied on the Advisor for substantially all services, with a Sponsor subsidiary serving as Property Manager, so the externally accessed processes and the organization operating them were structurally aligned rather than separated at closing. [SRC: SEC accession 0001567925-17-000028, Form 10-K FY2016]
